faqs.a: It checks each word against a bundled dictionary of common English words and computes edit-distance suggestions (up to 2 edits away) for anything it does not recognize.
faqs.q: How does this spell checker work?

faqs.a: Type in the box and misspelled words appear with a red wavy underline in the preview. Below it, each flagged word shows up to 5 suggestions as clickable buttons.
faqs.q: How do I see my mistakes?

faqs.a: Click any suggestion chip and every occurrence of that word in your text is replaced at once, preserving capitalization.
faqs.q: How do I apply a suggestion?

faqs.a: The dictionary is a compact list of common English words. Proper names, brands, slang and technical terms may be flagged even when spelled correctly.
faqs.q: Why is a correct word flagged?

faqs.a: Not currently. Suggestions come from the bundled dictionary only — there is no way to add custom words yet.
faqs.q: Can I add words to the dictionary?

faqs.a: Yes — everything is checked locally in your browser. Nothing you type is uploaded or stored anywhere.

spell-checker.formula:
misspelled = words not in DICTIONARY
suggestions(word) = dict words with levenshtein(word, candidate) <= 2
  sorted by distance, then alphabetically (top 5)

Misspelled words get a red wavy underline in the live preview, and each flagged word shows up to 5 suggestions as clickable chips — clicking one replaces every occurrence at once, preserving capitalization.

spell-checker.workedExample:
Input: "Please beleive me and adress this package"
Words checked: 7
- "beleive" not in dictionary -> flagged. Suggestions: believe, receive -> click "believe".
- "adress" not in dictionary -> flagged. Suggestions: address, dress, across, press, stress -> click "address".
Clicking a suggestion replaces every occurrence and keeps capitalization.
Result: "Please believe me and address this package"
Errors: 2 -> 0
mistakes: Accepting every suggestion blindly — 'their' vs 'there' are both valid words, and the wrong fix creates a new error.
Assuming it checks grammar — it flags spelling only, so broken sentences sail through untouched.
Pasting code — every variable and keyword gets flagged, burying the real typos in noise.
Ignoring dialect — US vs UK spelling ('color' vs 'colour') gets flagged as wrong when it is just different.
Trusting it with proper nouns — names and brand terms get flagged; do not 'correct' them into real words.
